Explanation

Your application has local or network IO operations.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, move persistent I/O to storage mounts (Azure Files/UNC). Keep local writes to temp only; connect to external dependencies via private endpoints/VNet to reduce latency.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Review and ensure IO APIs are attempting to access paths that will be available when your app is running on App Service sandbox. If you choose the containerized hosting option, your scenario still might be broken or have scalability issues.

Possible solutions:
1. Files that the application needs can be deployed with the application or put in Azure Storage. You can use Azure Storage File Shares as a drop-in replacement for on-premises file share.
2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.

Architecture Diagram

PhotoAlbum is a server-rendered photo gallery built with ASP.NET Core Razor Pages. The application uses a relational database for photo metadata and local disk storage for image files.

Data Storage & External Services

Photo metadata is stored in SQL Server LocalDB through Entity Framework Core, while image bytes are saved under the configured local upload directory. ImageSharp is used for dimension extraction; no cache, message broker, or external API integration is configured.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Razor Pages provide the server-side presentation layer and delegate photo operations to an injected service.
  • IPhotoService abstracts photo operations, while PhotoService coordinates file storage, image processing, and database persistence.
  • Upload configuration controls size, MIME types, and the local storage path.

DTOs & Contracts

UploadResult represents the internal outcome of a service upload operation. The upload page handler returns an anonymous JSON projection for successful uploads and upload errors; it is not declared as a dedicated DTO. Photo is the service-level domain entity used by the gallery and detail pages, and is also the metadata source for the photo-file response. These classes are mutable; no immutable request or response records, gateway-level DTOs, OpenAPI specification, protobuf schema, or GraphQL schema were found. JSON uses ASP.NET Core's default System.Text.Json serialization.

Communication Patterns

Page handlers call IPhotoService directly in-process. PhotoService uses EF Core for metadata operations and local filesystem operations for image bytes; there are no inter-service HTTP calls, message brokers, asynchronous event flows, service discovery, API gateway aggregation, or configured retry/circuit-breaker policies.

HTTPS redirection is enabled and HSTS is enabled outside Development. No authentication scheme or endpoint-specific authorization policy is configured. The authorization middleware is present in the request pipeline.

Core Business Workflows

PhotoAlbum lets users upload and browse a personal photo collection, inspect individual images, and remove photos. Its main business lifecycle is the coordination of image files and their corresponding metadata.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
PhotoPhotoAlbum / Photo ManagementA user-uploaded image and the metadata needed to display and manage itStored image file and metadata are coordinated by the photo-management context
UploadResultPhotoAlbum / Photo ManagementOutcome returned for an individual upload attemptReferences the created Photo by identifier on success

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
PhotoAlbumPhoto ManagementPhoto, UploadResultSQL Server for metadata; local filesystem for image bytes

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Upload Photos

  1. A user submits one or more files from the gallery.
  2. The upload handler rejects an empty submission; otherwise, it processes files individually through the photo service.
  3. The service checks the configured MIME-type allowlist and size limit, then rejects empty files.
  4. The service creates a unique stored filename and attempts to extract image dimensions. Dimension extraction failure is non-fatal.
  5. The image bytes are saved to local storage, and photo metadata is persisted.
  6. If metadata persistence fails after the file was written, the service attempts to delete the file as compensation. The handler returns a JSON summary of successful and failed files.

Workflow 2: Browse and View Photos

The gallery loads metadata in newest-first order. Selecting a photo loads its detail view and neighboring-photo identifiers. The photo-file route retrieves metadata, locates the stored image, and returns the file; missing metadata or a missing file results in not-found behavior.

Workflow 3: Delete a Photo

A user requests deletion from the detail view. The service loads the photo metadata, tries to delete its local file, and then removes its metadata from the database. A file deletion failure is logged but does not prevent database deletion; a database failure is propagated and the page redirects back with an error message.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no separate application services or cross-service aggregation flows. The PhotoAlbum service coordinates data between its metadata store and local file storage; the image file and its database record are associated through the stored filename.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Gallery User" participant Page as "Upload Page" participant Service as "Photo Service" participant Files as "Local Image Storage" participant Database as "Photo Metadata Store" User->>Page: Submit image files Page->>Service: Process each image Service->>Service: Check file type, size, and non-empty content alt File is not acceptable Service-->>Page: Rejected upload result Page-->>User: Include error in upload summary else File is acceptable Service->>Service: Generate stored name and inspect dimensions Service->>Files: Save image Service->>Database: Save photo metadata alt Metadata saved Database-->>Service: Created photo identifier Service-->>Page: Successful upload result Page-->>User: Return upload summary else Metadata save failed Database-->>Service: Persistence error Service->>Files: Attempt compensating file deletion Service-->>Page: Failed upload result Page-->>User: Include error in upload summary end end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Only configured image MIME types are accepted, and an upload must not exceed the configured maximum size or be empty.
  • Multiple submitted files are processed independently; the overall JSON result reports successful and failed files.
  • Image dimensions are optional metadata: inability to read dimensions does not prevent saving an otherwise acceptable image.
  • A generated unique stored filename is used for each saved image.
  • If metadata persistence fails after writing an image, the service attempts a compensating file deletion. Conversely, during photo deletion, file removal is best-effort and database removal proceeds even if the file cannot be deleted.
  • EF Core SaveChangesAsync is used for metadata changes; no explicit cross-resource transaction covers both the database and filesystem.
  • Failures are logged; upload failures are represented in the result, while unexpected deletion persistence failures are rethrown to the page handler.
  • No workflow-level authorization, audit trail, lifecycle state machine, or inter-service consistency mechanism was identified.

Caching Strategy

No server-side data cache or distributed cache provider is configured. Photo responses set HTTP cache headers, which affect client/proxy caching rather than EF Core query caching.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The single application owns its photo metadata database and local uploaded-file directory. There are no separate service data stores or cross-service data access paths. Reads and writes are performed directly through the DbContext and PhotoService; no CQRS or shared-database access between services was identified.
